stories.body: President Donald Trump said the United States is considering a possible attack on Iran as soon as Sunday, while also suggesting that negotiations with Tehran could still produce a major agreement.
stories.headline: Trump says US could attack Iran as soon as Sunday or reach a deal

stories.body: French authorities said nearly 1,000 people were arrested after hundreds of thousands joined nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living, school conditions and policing. Most marches were peaceful, but clashes broke out late in Paris and other cities, where police used tear gas, water cannon and baton charges; fires, barricades and vandalism were also reported. The government estimated turnout at about 410,000, while unions put it near 800,000.
stories.headline: Nearly 1,000 arrested after mass protests across France

stories.body: Brazilian voters are choosing between the 80-year-old left-wing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round 47% to 45%, but polls put the runoff race within the margin of error. Lula has framed the contest as a defense of democracy, while Bolsonaro has campaigned on tougher crime policies, spending cuts and a promise to seek his father's release from a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup.
stories.headline: Brazil votes in presidential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro

stories.body: Serbians are voting in snap parliamentary elections after nearly two years of student-led protests against corruption and authoritarianism, sparked by the 2024 collapse of a train-station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. Former president Aleksandar Vučić, who resigned to run for prime minister, faces a broad student movement whose platform centers on corruption and education. Polls indicate a close race, with one recent survey giving Vučić's party 47% to the student list's 40%.
stories.headline: Serbia votes in contest between Vučić and student-led opposition

stories.body: Israeli forces have imposed a lockdown on Hebron and displaced about 2,000 Palestinians after two Israeli soldiers were killed in an attack on an army reserve base. Israel's defense minister said residents would not be allowed to return until the military had dealt with what he described as Hamas activity in the city. The operation has included raids across the occupied West Bank, dozens of arrests and restrictions on Palestinian movement; the Palestinian Authority called the measures collective punishment and urged international intervention.
stories.headline: Israel displaces about 2,000 Palestinians in Hebron after attack on soldiers

stories.body: The Justice Department has asked a court to preemptively block Alaska's Senate result if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses, an extraordinary filing made less than two weeks before the midterms. Election-law experts from both parties said the move had little legal basis and viewed it as part of a broader Trump administration effort to exert federal influence over elections, including lawsuits for voter files and attempts to tie federal funding to state election practices. Trump said he personally approved the Alaska action, while the department said it was seeking to protect election integrity.
stories.headline: Justice Department seeks to block Alaska Senate result before election if Republican loses

stories.body: Former President Barack Obama criticized Donald Trump's administration over the Iran war, consumer prices and alleged corruption as he campaigned for Democrats in Ohio and Michigan before the November 3 midterms. Obama called the vote a chance to rein in an administration marked by "chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence," arguing that Trump had started an unnecessary war with Iran and failed to address rising costs. Trump, campaigning in Georgia, defended his tariffs and immigration policies and said the country was in a "golden age."
stories.headline: Obama denounces Trump's "cruelty and corruption" while campaigning for Democrats

stories.body: The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay more than $800 million to settle claims by about 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy, in what would be the second-largest such settlement in the United States. Archbishop Ronald Hicks said the agreement is to be formally signed November 6. Survivors are expected to receive at least $250,000 each, with higher payments possible depending on the abuse suffered.
stories.headline: New York Archdiocese agrees to $800 million settlement for abuse survivors

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said that, if the Socialists remain in government after Spain's November 29 election, they will amend the constitution to protect the right to abortion. Speaking at a campaign event in Granada, Sánchez said no man should control women's bodies, responding to opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo's suggestion that parental consent for 16-year-olds seeking abortions could be restored. Sánchez presented the election as a choice between progressive policies and cuts or reversals backed by the Popular Party and Vox.
stories.headline: Sánchez pledges to constitutionally protect abortion rights if reelected

stories.body: Spain's political parties are escalating their online campaigns ahead of the November 29 election with sharper personal attacks, memes and AI-generated videos. The Popular Party used AI to alter an image of Pedro Sánchez and to imitate figures associated with the Socialists, while Vox has followed a similar approach. Political communication experts say the campaign is more polarized and personal than previous contests, with viral attacks on opponents increasingly displacing debate over public policy.
stories.headline: AI-generated campaign videos intensify Spain's election battle

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez is campaigning on a warning that a Popular Party government supported by Vox would set Spain back decades, while Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo is centering his campaign on alleged Socialist corruption. At a rally in Vigo, Feijóo said he would not pardon corrupt figures and cited ongoing investigations involving the PSOE. Sánchez, seeking reelection after eight years in office, has cast the November 29 vote as a choice between social progress and a right-wing rollback of public services and rights.
stories.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo set opposing messages ahead of Spain's election

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra arrested about 100 people, including roughly 25 minors, after an unannounced youth protest in central Barcelona turned violent on Saturday evening. Authorities said groups set fires, vandalized street furniture, damaged shops and looted businesses near Plaça de Catalunya; at least 15 officers were injured and firefighters responded to 33 fires. Mayor Jaume Collboni and Interior Minister Núria Parlon condemned the violence, said it was unrelated to the housing encampment in the square, and promised legal action against both adult participants and the guardians of minors.
stories.headline: Barcelona police arrest about 100 people after central-city unrest

stories.body: The Catalan Education Assembly has approved a new cycle of strikes, beginning with a one-day stoppage on November 26, along with a demonstration on November 21 and participation in a general strike on November 11. The group is demanding more teachers, resources for inclusive education, smaller class sizes and improved pay and conditions. The decision follows a closely divided consultation in which 50.2% of participating education workers opposed further strikes, though the assembly said technical problems meant the poll did not reach much of the sector.
stories.headline: Catalan education assembly approves new strike cycle beginning November 26

stories.body: Barcelona plans to offer residents €400 toward new urban electric bicycles bought from December 1, with subsidies of up to €800 available for cargo e-bikes. The aid will be capped at 40% of the purchase price and applications are expected to open in 2027, although eligible purchases can begin this December. The city has allocated €4 million over four years and expects the program to support about 8,000 urban e-bikes and 800 cargo bikes.
stories.headline: Barcelona to offer €400 subsidies for electric bicycles bought from December

stories.body: Barcelona's 15 stormwater reservoirs all filled at once for the first time during heavy rain on October 3 and 4, when the city received 280 liters per square meter in four days, nearly half its usual annual rainfall. The underground and open-air reservoirs can hold nearly 500 million liters and are designed to prevent flooding by storing runoff until it can be released and treated. City officials said the event highlighted the need to expand the network, which is planned to grow from 15 to 29 reservoirs.
stories.headline: October rainfall fills all of Barcelona's stormwater reservoirs for first time
